flags: Crocs recorded $738.1 million in asset impairments in the second quarter of fiscal 2025, comprising a $430.0 million partial impairment of the HEYDUDE indefinite-lived trademark and a $307.0 million impairment of HEYDUDE Brand reporting unit goodwill, triggered by downward revisions to the internal HEYDUDE forecast.

The U.S. Supreme Court ruled that the President lacked authority to impose tariffs under IEEPA; the Court of International Trade subsequently ordered CBP to begin the refund process on March 4, 2026. Crocs estimated eligibility for approximately $75 million to $80 million in refunds and had received approximately $67 million by September 30, 2026.
Crocs' Board of Directors authorized an increase of the company's common stock repurchase authorization by $1.5 billion, bringing total remaining authorization to approximately $2.0 billion.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited item (P1, Item 1 Business)
business_model.claim: Crocs designs, develops, markets, distributes, and sells casual lifestyle footwear and accessories under two brands: the Crocs Brand (clogs, sandals, Jibbitz charms) and the HEYDUDE Brand (loafers and related products).
quotes: We are engaged in the design, development, worldwide marketing, distribution, and sale of casual lifestyle footwear and accessories for all.
We have two reportable operating segments: the Crocs Brand and the HEYDUDE Brand, which are discussed in more detail in "Business Segments and Geographic Information" below.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited item (P1, Item 1 Business)
business_model.claim: Products are sold in more than 85 countries through two distribution channels: wholesale (multi-brand retailers, mono-branded partner stores, e-tailers, distributors) and direct-to-consumer (company-operated e-commerce sites, third-party marketplaces, full-price retail stores, outlet stores, kiosks).
quotes: The broad appeal of our footwear has allowed us to market our products in more than 85 countries through two distribution channels: wholesale and direct-to-consumer ("DTC").

business_model.basis: stated in the cited item (P1, Item 1 Business)
business_model.claim: In fiscal year 2025, 47.9% of consolidated revenues came from the wholesale channel and 52.1% from the DTC channel.
quotes: During the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023, 47.9%, 50.3%, and 52.0% of our consolidated revenues, respectively, were derived through our wholesale channel.
During the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023, 52.1%, 49.7%, and 48.0%, respectively, of our consolidated revenues were derived through our DTC channel.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited item (P4, MD&A)
business_model.claim: Revenue is driven by unit sales volume, average selling price (ASP), channel mix, product mix, brand mix, and foreign currency fluctuations.
quotes: The increase was due to the net effects of: (i) higher unit sales volume in both brands, which resulted in an increase in revenues of $37.6 million, or 3.8%; (ii) higher average selling price on a constant currency basis ("ASP") driven by the Crocs Brand, which increased revenues by $9.0 million, or 0.9%; and (iii) net changes in exchange rates, which were approximately flat.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited item (P4, MD&A)
business_model.claim: In Q3 2026, Crocs Brand revenues grew 4.4% and HEYDUDE Brand revenues grew 6.1% year over year, with DTC growing faster than wholesale across both brands.
quotes: Crocs Brand revenues increased by 4.4% on a reported and constant currency basis, compared to the same period in 2025. HEYDUDE Brand revenues increased 6.1%, or 6.2% on a constant currency basis, compared to the same period in 2025.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited item (P3, MD&A)
business_model.claim: In fiscal year 2025, Crocs Brand revenues grew 1.5% while HEYDUDE Brand revenues decreased 13.3%, reflecting a period of weakness for HEYDUDE before the 2026 recovery.
quotes: We grew Crocs Brand revenues 1.5% compared to the same period in 2024. HEYDUDE Brand revenues decreased 13.3%.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited item (P3, MD&A)
business_model.claim: Cost of sales includes product manufacturing costs, distribution expenses (warehousing, transportation), and import duties; in 2025, distribution expenses alone were $488.4 million.
quotes: In the years ended December 31, 2025, and 2024, cost of sales included $488.4 million and $487.1 million, respectively, of distribution expenses primarily related to receiving, inspecting, warehousing, and packaging product in owned and third-party warehouses, combined with transportation costs associated with delivering products from distribution centers to wholesale partners, retail stores, and end customers.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited items (P3, P4)
business_model.claim: U.S. tariffs on imports from Vietnam, China, Indonesia, India, and Cambodia (ranging from 10% to 20%) are a significant cost driver, increasing product costs and compressing gross margin.
quotes: the United States ("U.S.") has imposed tariffs on foreign imports from multiple countries, including, most relevant to us, an incremental tariff of 20%, 20%, 19%, 18%, and 19% on all imports from Vietnam, China, Indonesia, India, and Cambodia, respectively.
Gross margin was 58.3% compared to 58.8% in 2024, a decrease of 50 basis points, primarily due to unfavorable duties for both brands as a result of the aforementioned incremental tariffs.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited item (P4, MD&A)
business_model.claim: In Q3 2026, the company recorded approximately $64 million of IEEPA tariff refund benefit in cost of sales, contributing 630 basis points to the 770-basis-point gross margin expansion year over year.
quotes: Of this amount, approximately $64 million of benefit is recorded within 'Cost of sales' and approximately $3 million of benefit is recorded within 'Interest income' in the condensed consolidated statements of operations during the three months ended September 30, 2026.

Gross margin increased in the three months ended September 30, 2026, to 66.2% compared to 58.5% in the same period in 2025, primarily due to IEEPA refunds of 630 basis points, lower duties of 130 basis points, favorable channel mix of 70 basis points, and lower product costs in the Crocs Brand of 40 basis points, partially offset by unfavorable product mix in the Crocs Brand of 130 basis points.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited items (P4, P3)
business_model.claim: SG&A is driven by compensation, marketing spend, DTC channel costs (rent, marketplace fees), and periodic cost-savings or restructuring charges.
quotes: SG&A increased $22.5 million, or 6.0%, during the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to the same period in 2025, primarily due to higher DTC costs of $9.2 million, driven by increased share of marketplaces and rent expense as a result of investments in the channel.
SG&A were $1,469.4 million compared to $1,364.3 million 2024, primarily as a result of increased investment in talent and higher costs in the DTC channel.
